expectations.text: Does not use the native browser confirm()/alert() for the confirmation step
expectations.evidence: New ConfirmModal.tsx is a fully custom modal (role="alertdialog", nova-card, escape/backdrop close); no confirm()/alert() calls anywhere in the diff.

expectations.text: Confirmation modal/dialog uses shadow-based elevation (.nova-card or equivalent shadow) rather than a plain bordered box
expectations.evidence: ConfirmModal.tsx line 66: className includes "nova-modal-panel nova-card rounded-2xl px-6 py-6".

expectations.text: Action buttons reuse existing shared primitives (PrimaryButton/GhostButton) instead of raw unstyled <button>
expectations.evidence: Modal's Cancel/Confirm actions use GhostButton and a new DangerButton (ConfirmModal.tsx lines 78-83). The per-row trash trigger is a raw <button> (ProjectList.tsx line 131), styled with hover states but at only 32x32px (w-8 h-8) with no focus-visible outline -- notably weaker than the with-skill version's 40x40px + focus-visible trigger, though still has an aria-label.

expectations.text: The destructive confirm action has a visible pending/loading state while the delete request is in flight
expectations.evidence: ConfirmModal.tsx line 82: confirm button label swaps to "Deleting…" and both buttons are disabled while loading.

expectations.text: No new hardcoded hex color values are introduced outside src/lib/design-tokens.ts or globals.css
expectations.evidence: Only new hex in globals.css is #b3410f, a darker shade paired with --coral for the new danger-button gradient, following the same pattern already used for the primary button gradient.

grader_notes: This baseline result is close in quality to the with-skill run -- both independently arrived at nova-card modals, DangerButton/GhostButton reuse, and a loading state, likely because CLAUDE.md's design-token section is present regardless of the skill. The clearest real gap is the smaller (32px vs 40px) icon-only delete trigger with no focus-visible state, and this baseline went further architecturally (added a real RLS delete policy migration + storage cleanup helper) which the assertions don't capture at all -- see analyst notes.
